messages:
maya: quick note — ran a head-to-head client loadtest (gRPC vs REST) for the new kernel-selection patch. Synthetic harness + replay both. Seeing big 95/99 tails when keepalive is off and when pool size is small.

ben: ugh yup, we hit this before. common culprits: keepalive disabled, small connection pool, Nagle on (no TCP_NODELAY), TLS handshake on every request. what config did you use?

maya: small snippet of what I ran:
```
# replay harness (python loadgen)
clients=200
concurrency=200
mode=replay
keepalive=false
api=grpc (http2) / rest (http1.1)
```
I toggled keepalive true/false and saw median similar but p95/p99 jumped ~3-4x with keepalive=false.

liam: can you share exact wrk/hey commands? race conditions with HTTP/2 multiplexing can look better on medians but hide per-connection TLS or Nagle stalls at tails.

maya: sure — quick `wrk` run for REST: 
```
w rk -t12 -c400 -d60 --latency http://gateway/sync?model=x
```
for gRPC I used our python harness with `grpcio` and `--http2` flag on the driver.

nisha: two other gotchas we saw: 1) KV cache warm vs cold — replaying real traffic warms local KV and hides prefix cache misses in synthetic tests. 2) kernel selection regressions — when the runtime picks the int8 path for short seq lengths it sometimes adds dequant/pack overhead that increases latency for tiny requests. make sure your harness has both short and long sequences.

maya: good call on kv warm. I ran a cold sweep and p99 exploded on chat-like short msgs. with a warm prefix cache p99 improved ~2.1x. noted for the benchmark doc.

ben: for apples-to-apples:
- always run warmup phase (eg 30s) to populate caches
- fix client keepalive and pool settings in both gRPC and REST runs
- record connection counts + TLS handshake rate
- run a matrix across seq lengths and batch sizes
- capture kernel selection logs from the runtime (which kernel chosen + reason)

liam: small example settings we use in load harness:
```
client: {
  keepalive: true,
  pool_size: concurrency * 2,
  idle_conn_timeout_ms: 30000,
  tcp_nodelay: true,  # disable Nagle
}
server: {
  kv_cache: prewarm=true,
  kernel_log_level: info
}
```
this reduced p99 by ~30% in our last run.

maya: interesting: when I forced `tcp_nodelay=false` I saw clustering of tail latencies at multiples of ~40ms — looks like delayed ACK/Nagle interactions.

nisha: TLS+Nagle is the worst for small request sizes. TLS handshake per-request killed us in non-keepalive runs. also some HTTP/2 gRPC clients open fewer connections and rely on multiplexing — that hides TLS cost but can create head-of-line stalls if one request blocks long-running decoding.

ben: another perf regression we discovered earlier: the kernel selector prioritized a fused matmul kernel that assumed contiguous KV layout; under certain batch shapes it did extra copying, adding ~6-8% tail. add batch-shape specific microbenchmarks.

maya: profile snapshot from the run (abbreviated):
```
# perf top sample:
35% matmul_fused_int8 (pack/dequant)
18% rsa_tls_handshake
12% grpc_io (parse)
9% kv_cache_lookup
6% batch_scheduler
```
shows both kernel overhead and TLS cost.

liam: solid. plan: 1) update load harness README w/ keepalive/pool best practices 2) add warm/cold KV scenarios to all regression tests 3) add small microbench job sweeping seq len vs kernel path 4) instrument client side to emit conn/reuse stats.

dev-bot: [load-harness] nightly-run #452 finished — artifacts: s3://redwood-harness/172/452/{latency.csv,kernel_log.txt,conn_metrics.json}

maya: thanks — I'll attach those to the perf ticket. can we also make the default demo scripts set `tcp_nodelay: true` and `keepalive: true` so new users don't shoot themselves in the foot? :thumbsup:

nisha: yes please. also add a short checklist: warmup, pool>=concurrency, disable Nagle, capture kernel selection, run cold/warm KV. small doc PR incoming.

ben: one more note — when comparing gRPC vs REST, ensure payload framing is identical (proto vs json) and measure server-side CPU breakdown. gRPC can be better for throughput but sometimes worse for tail latency in our stack depending on deserialization hotspots.

maya: agreed. next steps: update harness config, add matrix tests (seq len x batch size x keepalive), and run full comparison tomorrow. thanks all.
